kind: constructed synthetic portfolios with fixture-author expectations; no human labels
method: Executed: the prototype functions in apps/desktop/test/outcome-gap-research run on the portfolios in fixtures.ts. Expected verdicts, reasons and suggestion sets were declared by the fixture author from the written rules before the code was run.
Executed: invariances (what must not change when outcomes, scores or assessments change) and a dismissal check.
Executed, constructed: five simpler rules scored on the same fixture (baselines).
Source reading: the manual-review side of the desk comparison.
Real-contract lane (added by evaluation.test.ts): synthetic data written through the app’s real writers into a migrated database and read back by the read-only adapter.
Review gates are author-declared and not statistically derived (GATES in contract.ts). No inference is made about any real person.

portfolios.title: Enough data, if follow-ups A and B existed
portfolios.what: 30 requisitions: 34 source rows (4 syndicated pairs), 3 sources and 3 query variants recorded, 22 mature sends with 8 unknown outcomes, 20 current assessments, a lead-exposure digest and dated status events. NOT what the app records today.

portfolios.title: What today’s records look like
portfolios.what: 8 requisitions in the exact shape the real adapter returns: no query attribution, current-value status, no exposure, 3 assessments (1 stale), 1 prepared-only, 1 too-recent send, 1 undated send.

portfolios.title: Saved copies dominate
portfolios.what: 22 mature sends, each saved 4 times by the person (88 saved rows for 22 requisitions: savedRowsCollapsed 66, aliasContributionsMerged 0).

portfolios.title: Source copies merged before saving dominate
portfolios.what: 22 mature sends, each saved ONCE but merged from 4 source copies by brief aliases (22 saved rows, 88 source contributions): savedRowsCollapsed 0, aliasContributionsMerged 66, copiesSeen 88. The duplicate gate fires without claiming that any of those copies was a saved copy.

portfolios.title: Most outcomes are unknown
portfolios.what: 24 mature sends, 20 with no recorded outcome.

portfolios.title: Identity is mostly the weak tier
portfolios.what: 22 mature sends keyed only by company/title/location text.

portfolios.title: Assessments made against three different CV versions
portfolios.what: 12 current assessments over CV hashes 5/4/3: the evidence classes are not comparable across CV versions.

portfolios.title: Assessments summarised under another rule version or an unknown one
portfolios.what: 12 current assessments: 3 under the current rules, 6 under an older rule version, 3 with no recorded version.

portfolios.title: Kubernetes / K8s: merged only by the person
portfolios.what: 10 current assessments; "Kubernetes" in 2, "K8s" in 2, "Kube" in 1. Without a person-confirmed alias no wording reaches the recurrence threshold of 3; the person confirming that they are one thing makes it 5.

portfolios.title: Two roles at one employer and a reapplication
portfolios.what: 3 requisitions at the same employer; one was applied for twice. Each role keeps its own requirement lane and outcome.

outcomesFlipped.claim: Making every sent application rejected, or every one an interview, changes no requirement row, no lane count, no eligibility row and no suggestion; only the labelled outcome context moves.

scoresChanged.claim: Setting every fit score to missing, to 0, or to 99 changes no requirement row and no suggestion. A score of 0 is a recorded score and is counted as scored; missing is counted as unscored.

actual.note: An evaluator opinion about fit. It is not a requirement, a gap or an outcome, and it is not used to compute any row here.

allMissing.note: An evaluator opinion about fit. It is not a requirement, a gap or an outcome, and it is not used to compute any row here.

allZero.note: An evaluator opinion about fit. It is not a requirement, a gap or an outcome, and it is not used to compute any row here.

noAssessmentMeansNoRequirements.claim: Removing every assessment leaves the same job titles, scores and outcomes but no requirement row and no requirement suggestion; nothing is inferred from the rest.

titlesAndScorerHintsChanged.claim: Planting "Kubernetes" in every job title and every scorer hint, or blanking them all, changes no requirement row, no lane count and no suggestion. The unassessed jobs stay unknown.

titleOnlyNegativeControl.claim: The titles_only_no_assessment portfolio contains jobs TITLED Kubernetes with Kubernetes scorer hints and no assessment. The prototype yields no requirement row and no requirement suggestion and counts every job as not assessed; a leaky rule that read titles or hints would not.

classificationMatters.claim: The recurrence threshold counts every assessed appearance whatever its class; every row and suggestion states the required / preferred / unclear split; a row that is only preferred never gets mandatory wording; the split is a posting-side fact and moves no row, lane or threshold when changed.

allPreferredRow.subject: On-call rota
allPreferredRow.statement: “On-call rota” appears in 3 of the 20 assessed jobs you chose (listed only as preferred, a nice-to-have, in all 3), and your CV has no recorded evidence for it in those. If you have this experience, you may want to add it to your CV yourself; if you do not, that is for you to decide. The postings list it only as a nice-to-have, so how much it matters is for you to judge.

mixedRow.subject: Kubernetes
mixedRow.statement: “Kubernetes” appears in 5 of the 20 assessed jobs you chose (required in 3, preferred in 1, unclear in 1), and your CV has no recorded evidence for it in those. If you have this experience, you may want to add it to your CV yourself; if you do not, that is for you to decide.

dismissal.claim: A dismissed suggestion leaves the visible list, stays inspectable, does not return when more supporting jobs arrive (it reports how many newer ones), and dismissing changes no suggestion and no input.

baselines.note: Constructed comparisons on the rich_projected portfolio only. Each is a simpler rule someone might write; none is shipped behaviour.

titleKeywordGap.note: Computed from the fixture titles: only unassessed jobs whose own title says Kubernetes. Unassessed jobs with other titles are unknown, not title-derived.

scorerHintGap.note: The scorer’s matching skills and "gaps" compare a job with the person’s stated profile and preferences; they are not skill gaps and are never read as requirements.

method: Fixture: the rich_projected portfolio (30 requisitions) with invented free text on some jobs (kept Fit check, next step, notes, #691 round notes, #692 follow-up text).
MANUAL side = SOURCE READING of what the current screens show (file citations below). Nothing was executed on the manual side and no person was observed.
PROTOTYPE side = EXECUTED: one run of the views on the same fixture.

Unit = DISTINCT RECORDS a person would open or screens they would read. A record is counted once however many questions it answers (a saved-job drawer opened once answers Q1, Q2 and Q3); per-question counts are shown separately and are NOT added into a headline. It is not time, effort, accuracy or a usability result. No human labels were collected; the "better" column is the fixture author’s reading.

Like-for-like: the prototype can only answer a question for a job that was ALREADY assessed ("Compare with my CV"); the structured part of the brief needs the same prerequisite. The assessments, and the model run behind each kept Fit check, are not counted on either side. The prototype therefore saves no assessment work and these counts are not a time or usability saving.
The rich portfolio is projected data. Where the answer needs a field production does not record, the row says so and the comparison is of design capability, not of what the app does today.

surfaces.savedJobDrawer: apps/desktop/src/components/saved/SavedJobDrawer.tsx: ONE drawer per saved job shows the kept "Fit check" free text AND the brief panel (requirement evidence, recorded-gap vs open-question lists capped at BRIEF_LIST_CAP = 5, eligibility, "Where this came from"). Opening it once answers Q1, Q2, Q3 and the source half of Q4.
surfaces.gapAnalysis: apps/desktop/src/components/cv/GapAnalysis.tsx + gap-analysis-store.ts (saveGapAnalysis): the CV-assistant flow that PRODUCES the kept Fit check. It runs the person’s own CLI/model once per job and "Save analysis" stores the free text on the saved job, with no posting or CV version. That run is the origin of the kept Fit check and is not counted below; the prototype runs no model.
surfaces.table: apps/desktop/src/components/applications/ApplicationsTable.tsx (ONE screen lists every application with its status and Next step)
surfaces.applicationDrawer: apps/desktop/src/components/applications/ApplicationDrawer.tsx (notes, next step, contact; one drawer per application)
surfaces.interviewRounds: apps/desktop/src/components/applications/InterviewRoundsPanel.tsx, shown in InterviewPrepDrawer.tsx (#691): per-round state, feedback and open topics, free text
surfaces.followUps: apps/desktop/src/components/applications/FollowUpsDrawer.tsx and FollowUpDraftCard.tsx (#692): dated follow-up actions (title, note) and drafts, free text
surfaces.found: apps/desktop/src/components/search/VacancyDetail.tsx ("Found with": queries, shown only for a lead in the latest scan report)

totals.prerequisiteForPrototype: 20 of 30 jobs had to be assessed ("Compare with my CV") first; 10 are reported as unknown
totals.note: Distinct records and screens, not time. A prototype run reads data that must already exist, so on today’s data q4 is a no-go and q1-q3 depend on how many jobs the person assessed. These counts are not a time or usability saving and no single "N by hand versus M by prototype" ratio is offered.

limits: No human did any of this; the manual side is a reading of the source, the prototype side is a run on constructed data.
A person with 3 saved jobs does not need an aggregate: the counted advantage only appears as the number of jobs grows.

Free text (notes, next step, round feedback, follow-up text, the kept Fit check) can carry the decisive fact. The prototype ignores it on purpose, so it is complementary to manual review, not a replacement.
The assessments the prototype needs, and the model run behind each kept Fit check, are real work that this comparison does not count on either side.
No claim is made about decision quality, time saved, hiring outcomes or user preference.

unknowns: No human labels: every expected value was written by the implementer. Nothing here is human validated.
No real job search was used. The portfolios say nothing about how often these patterns occur for a real person, employer or ATS.
Nothing is known about whether any suggestion would be useful, understood or acted on; no usability study was run.
The rich portfolio relies on fields production does not record (query attribution, status events, exposure counts); its go_review verdicts describe the contract, not the app.
The review gates (counts and shares) are author-declared. They were not tuned or validated on data and could be wrong in either direction.
Maturity (28 days) has no empirical basis; employers answer on very different time scales and many never answer.
Exact-text recurrence under-counts spelling variants; person-confirmed aliases fix that only for wordings the person notices.
No provider, token, latency or cost telemetry was collected or is claimed: nothing in the prototype calls a model.
limits: Selected jobs are survivorship-filtered: the aggregate describes the jobs and applications the person KEPT. Deleting a saved job removes it only when no application row still keeps the requisition; deleting the application as well removes it entirely.

The recurrence threshold counts required, preferred and unclear appearances alike; the split is always shown, but a posting-side class is still the extraction’s reading of the posting, not a verified fact.

Evidence classes direct / transferable / unsupported / needs_verification are model-proposed and then person-reviewed (the record does not say whether the person changed the class); only candidate_confirmed_gap is the person’s own statement.
Correlation between a requirement and an outcome is never presented as cause; outcomes are context only.
A requirement a CV cannot evidence is not a missing skill.
The conclusion is about whether automated calibration is supportable (it is not), not about hiring outcomes.

unrecoverable.detail: No workspace table or brief column stores which query variant produced a saved job (LeadQueryProvenance exists only in the scan report JSON).
Leads shown, skipped or ignored are not stored; only jobs the person saved or applied to exist.
applications.status is one mutable value with no change time, source or reason; the only application date is applied_at.

Deleting a saved job removes its row (and a brief nothing else references). An application row made from it survives (applications.saved_job_id is set to null) and keeps the requisition; only when the application is deleted too does the requisition disappear. If no attempt references the brief it goes with the saved job and the surviving application is re-keyed from its stored text (weak tier). What the person dropped is therefore invisible, so "selected" describes the jobs and applications the person kept.
cv_documents keeps no version history; a CV or JD version is only a hash, so compatibility is hash equality, not a diff.
